School Fair

School Fair (Findlay Buchanan, Semisi Ma’ia’i, Hamish Morgan, De Stevens and Rose Pickernell) make music embedded in the human experience. It’s a product of the band’s native New Zealand, a place that remains intimate and remote, where emotion is magnified over both distance and familiarity. The five band members began the project renting out a factory-sized, sub-zero degree Celsius room normally operated by construction workers in the industrial area of Ōtepoti, Dunedin, New Zealand in 2021, recording music on the 4-track tape recorder that would become debut Gorse on a Hill. The album remained the only trace of the band online for a few years, an artifact for those who know where to look. School Fair’s music has this sense of self-discovery when you find it, a sound that feels both recognizable and like the vacant expanse of a country whirring by on a train. Still with little to no self-promotion, the appearance of sophomore effort Bird the Kid online in early 2025 was a new portal to their world of melodic and intricate indie music that retains a kind of atmospheric beauty.

Unexpected Violence (Mutual, 2026) is the first record made between geographical places, with the band now split in between London and New Zealand. You can hear this fragmented approach in the patchwork quality and inherent connective tissue of the album. Weaving together chamber classical, folk, torch song, and experimental music, Dorian Wood’s Canto de Todes is a 70-minute distillation born from Wood’s acclaimed 12-hour composition and installation. The title—Spanish for “Song of Everyone”—is inspired by a lyric of the late Chilean singer and songwriter Violeta Parra. Canto de Todes emphasizes the urgency of music as a vessel for social change, and honors the ancestral trajectory of Wood’s Costa Rican-Nicaraguan family and their experience in the U.S.

Dorian Wood (b. 1975, pronouns: she/her/they/them) is an anti-disciplinary artist based in the U.S., whose practice seeks to “infect” spaces and ideologies in order to challenge traditions and systems of marginalization. Her performances, films and visual works have been presented worldwide. From 2019–2020, Wood toured internationally with XAVELA LUX AETERNA, a chamber orchestra tribute to Chavela Vargas. Subsequent works Mares Ocultos (2022), a compositional series centering on deconstructing male heterosexuality.

Born in San Juan, Puerto Rico, Roco Córdova is a vocalist, composer, producer and improviser based in the San Francisco Bay Area. They possess a B.Mus. in Composition from the Puerto Rico Conservatory of Music and an M.A. in Composition from Mills College in Oakland, California. events.title: Krs One
events.description:
Appearing on the rap scene in 1986 as Boogie Down Productions, releasing his first hit single “South Bronx” with his late DJ Scott La Rock, KRS “the one” made it clear that Hip Hop was going to have to take itself a lot more seriously than simply being a music genre.

KRS, an acronym for “Knowledge Reigning Supreme”, has been called the “conscience of Hip Hop” (Rolling Stone), “the greatest live emcee ever” (The Source), the “spokesperson for Hip Hop” (Wall Street Journal), “master teacher” (Zulu Nation) and the “son of Hip Hop” (Kool DJ Herc).

With 20 published albums to his credit and his numerous appearances with other artists, KRS-One is believed to have written the most rhymes in Hip Hop’s history. In the 1990s, as “hip-hop” grew more and more commercialized and corporate, it was KRS-One that openly rejected such cultural exploitation and materialism, grounding Hip Hop in its original principles of peace, love, unity, and safely having fun. Teaching everything from self-creation to stopping violence; from vegetarianism to transcendental meditation, from the establishment of Hip Hop Appreciation Week (every third week in May), to establishing Hip Hop as an international culture at the United Nations (2001), KRS-One has single-handedly held the history and original arts of Hip Hop together now for over two decades.

In addition to lecturing at over 500 universities in the United States and publishing three ground-breaking books; “The Science of Rap” (1995), “Ruminations”...

The Moth is dedicated to finding people from all walks of life to tell inspired stories. At The Moth StorySLAM, those people find us. On this night, winners from our StorySLAM series compete to determine The San Francisco GrandSLAM Story Champion.

The Moth GrandSLAM is the ultimate storytelling championship, inviting winners from The Moth’s open-mic StorySLAMs back to the stage to battle for the crown. With a full slate of local storytelling pros, you know this night is going to be good. Come experience fierce, hilarious, and sometimes even heartbreaking stories at the Moth GrandSLAM live.

The Moth is a global storytelling nonprofit with the mission to inspire people to listen and share openly, think and feel deeply, and expand their understanding of one another. Since 1997, The Moth has presented more than 70,000 true stories—told live and without notes—in 11 countries, across 4 continents. Today, The Moth produces 600+ live shows annually, as well as the Peabody Award-winning The Moth Radio Hour, and the popular The Moth Podcast. Through workshops for students, educators, adults, advocates, and professionals, The Moth guides thousands of new storytellers each year in finding and sharing their own voices. After five transformative years, Rashad delivers his most vulnerable and fully-realized work yet — an unfiltered reflection on addiction, growth, self-confrontation, and redemption. It’s soul music in its most metaphysical form, anchored by the same lyrical precision and emotional depth that have defined his artistry from the beginning.

Since emerging from Chattanooga, TN in 2012, Rashad has built one of the most impactful and emotionally resonant catalogs in modern rap. His debut Cilvia Demo immediately established him as a critical force, followed by The Sun’s Tirade, which debuted in the Top 20 of the Billboard 200 and earned Gold certification. His 2021 album The House Is Burning further solidified his cultural imprint, amassing nearly one billion global streams and widespread acclaim for its introspective storytelling and sonic evolution. events.title: Fermenting Hope
events.description:
Fermenting Hope invites the public into a live vertical dance investigation about creativity, fermentation and hope.

What if hope isn't just a feeling, but something we practice? What has to break down for something new to emerge?

Over a four-day residency at Faction Brewing, choreographer Amelia Rudolph explores these questions with seven dancers in the brewery's towering industrial space. Amelia Rudolph is a vertical dance innovator and the founder of BANDALOOP. Her seven dancers work alongside an original score by composer Luke Mombrea and sculptural design by Todd Laby. Like fermentation, the process is open-ended: the artists set the conditions and let the work take shape.

The residency culminates in a public showing, a chance to see new work as it emerges. Afterward, Jon Moscone, Radium Arts Artistic Director, leads a guided conversation with the artists and public about the creative process.

Free and open to all ages. Nov. 13 7:00 PM * Faction Brewing, Alameda Point

Fermenting Hope is made possible by a generous grant from the City of Alameda Public Art Program.

Free

Presented by Radium Arts

events.title: All About My Mother
events.description:
Presented in Spanish with English subtitles

Though Pedro Almodóvar’s films have pushed the boundaries of cinema as far back as the mid-1970s, it wasn’t until 1999’s ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER that the Academy Awards finally took notice, naming it the Best Foreign Language Film of the year. And it serves as a perfect encapsulation of his enduring power as an artist: it’s colorful, dynamic, emotional, darkly funny, and imbued with profound empathy.

When tragedy strikes, Manuela (Cecilia Roth, PEPI, LUCI, BOM) travels to Barcelona for the first time in years in search of someone from her past. But she is waylaid by her old friend Agrado (Antonia San Juan), a transgender sex worker, as well as new friends, such as Hermana (Penélope Cruz, PAIN AND GLORY), a nun with a secret, and Huma (Marisa Paredes, THE SKIN I LIVE IN), an actress performing in town. Together, the women form a unique bond that carries them through the challenges that life throws at them.

Driven by the powerhouse performances of each actress in the film, ALL ABOUT MY MOTHER showcases the humanity of these women at their best and worst, their highest and lowest, resulting in a portrait of friendship, family, and love that is singularly Almodóvar.

events.title: Kino
events.description: Born in the underground clubs of Leningrad in 1981, KINO became the defining voice of Soviet rock — a band that smuggled freedom into every chord when freedom itself was contraband. Fronted by the magnetic Viktor Tsoi, they played to 62,000 at Moscow's Luzhniki Stadium in 1990. Months later, Tsoi was gone. The music never stopped. "What Elvis Presley was to America, Tsoi was to Russia." Now, original members Yuri Kasparyan, Alexander Titov, and Igor Tikhomirov bring KINO back to the stage — accompanied by Tsoi's own voice, restored and digitized from original multi-track recordings. This is not a tribute act. This is KINO, continuing the conversation. Expect anthems you know by heart — Gruppa Krovi, Peremen, Posledniy Geroy — performed with the raw urgency that made them timeless. Sung in Russian. Felt in every language.

events.title: “It’s Raining Queens”
events.description:
A powerhouse evening of music, comedy and storytelling arrives this fall as legendary vocalist Martha Wash and comedian and actress Marsha Warfield unite for It’s Raining Queens at Feinstein’s at the Nikko on November 13.

For both performers, the engagement marks a meaningful homecoming to the city tied to the early chapters of their careers.

Martha Wash was born and raised in San Francisco, where her journey began. She first gained recognition singing alongside Sylvester as one half of Two Tons O’ Fun before achieving international success with The Weather Girls. A two-time Grammy nominee, Wash is the voice behind multi-platinum recordings with The Weather Girls, Black Box and C+C Music Factory, a catalog that shaped dance floors and pop radio around the world and continues to inspire new generations.

Warfield’s San Francisco connection dates to a pivotal breakthrough. In 1979, she won the San Francisco International Comedy Competition, becoming the contest’s first Black winner and its first female winner. She went on to write and perform for Richard Pryor’s groundbreaking variety series The Richard Pryor Show before building her own reputation on sharp, unhurried wit. An Emmy and NAACP Image Award nominee, she is best known for Night Court and has since appeared on The Upshaws and 9-1-1.

events.title: Krs One
events.description:
Appearing on the rap scene in 1986 as Boogie Down Productions, releasing his first hit single “South Bronx” with his late DJ Scott La Rock, KRS “the one” made it clear that Hip Hop was going to have to take itself a lot more seriously than simply being a music genre.

KRS, an acronym for “Knowledge Reigning Supreme”, has been called the “conscience of Hip Hop” (Rolling Stone), “the greatest live emcee ever” (The Source), the “spokesperson for Hip Hop” (Wall Street Journal), “master teacher” (Zulu Nation) and the “son of Hip Hop” (Kool DJ Herc).

With 20 published albums to his credit and his numerous appearances with other artists, KRS-One is believed to have written the most rhymes in Hip Hop’s history. In the 1990s, as “hip-hop” grew more and more commercialized and corporate, it was KRS-One that openly rejected such cultural exploitation and materialism, grounding Hip Hop in its original principles of peace, love, unity, and safely having fun. Teaching everything from self-creation to stopping violence; from vegetarianism to transcendental meditation, from the establishment of Hip Hop Appreciation Week (every third week in May), to establishing Hip Hop as an international culture at the United Nations (2001), KRS-One has single-handedly held the history and original arts of Hip Hop together now for over two decades.

In addition to lecturing at over 500 universities in the United States and publishing three ground-breaking books; “The Science of Rap” (1995), “Ruminations”...

In a trio formation with some of the core rhythm section players from the record, Max Jaffe, Gavin Gamboa, and Logan Kane reimagine the music from Jaffe's 2025 release You Want That Too!

Max Jaffe is a drummer, producer, composer, and technologist based in Los Angeles, CA. His work expands the possibilities of composition and collaboration through the drum set.

In 2025, Jaffe released "You Want That Too!" on Colorfield Records. Eclectic and tuneful, the album received praise from Pitchfork and is being followed with a series of special live performances in varying formations.

Max is a founding member of experimental rock collective JOBS, Amirtha Kidambi's Elder Ones, and several others. Burden of Dreams is the latest band from Oakland composer and multi-instrumentalist, Nathan Clevenger. events.title: The Searchers
events.description:
A favorite film of some of the world's greatest filmmakers, including Martin Scorsese and Steven Spielberg, THE SEARCHERS has earned its place in the legacy of great American films for a variety of reasons. Perhaps most notably, it's the definitive role for John Wayne as an icon of the classic Western – the hero (or antihero) who must stand alone according to the unwritten code of the West.

As with many of Ford's classic Westerns, THE SEARCHERS must contend with revisionism in its stereotypical treatment of "savage" Native Americans, and the film's visual beauty (the final shot is one of the great images in all of Western culture) is compromised by some uneven performances and stilted dialogue. Still, this is undeniably one of the greatest Westerns ever made.

events.title: San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival 2026: First Program
events.description:
The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival returns to the Bay Area to celebrate locally-made cinematic mayhem!

Founded by Peaches Christ & Vinsantos in 2003 at the Bridge Theatre, partially as a showcase for their own short films that weren’t getting traction at “legitimate” festivals, the SFUSFF ran under their care for six years until 2008. After Vinsantos moved to New Orleans, Peaches and fellow film programmer Sam Sharkland wanted to see the fest continue and so revived it in 2011 at the Victoria Theatre where it ran until 2015. Now, after 10 years, the festival has found a new home at the 4 Star Theater under the care of Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X, the maniacal minds behind Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival exists to celebrate local, independent filmmaking. We proudly champion the overlooked and underrated, the avant-garde and the alternative, the outrageous, the oddball, and the outlandish. We'll be presenting the silly, subversive, surreal, and strange from all Bay Area filmmakers! From bizarro B-films to midnight movie trash, expect the weirdest and wildest the Bay has to offer, with the night kicking off with our lighter fare and getting darker and more freaky as the evening goes on. Cinematic weirdos - you have found the festival for you!

The language we speak is something we learned, which means we can learn to communicate differently — moving what now feels impossible to say into the realm of the possible. Language Alchemy® helps you discover your authentic expression for the benefit of all, so that the way you speak and relate becomes a model for the present and the future.

• Hear an excerpt from the book on maturing our language to match our own growth and development
• Leave with a new way of understanding communication as a practice of building meaningful relationships

events.title: San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival 2026: Second Program
events.description:
The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival returns to the Bay Area to celebrate locally-made cinematic mayhem!

Founded by Peaches Christ & Vinsantos in 2003 at the Bridge Theatre, partially as a showcase for their own short films that weren’t getting traction at “legitimate” festivals, the SFUSFF ran under their care for six years until 2008. After Vinsantos moved to New Orleans, Peaches and fellow film programmer Sam Sharkland wanted to see the fest continue and so revived it in 2011 at the Victoria Theatre where it ran until 2015. Now, after 10 years, the festival has found a new home at the 4 Star Theater under the care of Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X, the maniacal minds behind Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival exists to celebrate local, independent filmmaking. We proudly champion the overlooked and underrated, the avant-garde and the alternative, the outrageous, the oddball, and the outlandish. We'll be presenting the silly, subversive, surreal, and strange from all Bay Area filmmakers! From bizarro B-films to midnight movie trash, expect the weirdest and wildest the Bay has to offer, with the night kicking off with our lighter fare and getting darker and more freaky as the evening goes on. Cinematic weirdos - you have found the festival for you!

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia Opening Reception
events.description:
Larisa Brechun: Somnia
Opening Reception with the artist 5–9 PM

The subtle qualities of the soul—softness, stillness, fragility, solitude—are often belittled for their “weakness," dismissed as defects of simpering prey in a predatory age, where might and volume rule and humanity fills its hours with chatter and self-exposure. Introspection is the enemy of the social machine, softness a death sentence, silence a grave. And yet, these delicate instincts are essential to the most intimate operation of the soul: the dream.

In Larisa Brechuns’s Somnia, the artist lays bare the quiet privacy of the dreaming mind and the fugitive debris of memory, myth, and imagination as it freely floats in the cocoon of sleep, coalescing into mysterious forms that defy daylight logic. Under her gentle hand, soft animal bodies take shape alongside evaporating cosmic beings and primordial symbols of wilderness, all adrift in the penumbra of the dreaming state, suspended in etheric margins between the deep woodland dark and the flirting light of a winking moon.

Brechun’s darkness has substance, an amplitude of unseen marrow with texture and weight, like a cave or a chrysalis. Lonely figures gently emerge from abyssal thickets, twisting into the light of the omnipresent moon’s awareness as quickly as they recede. They are camouflaged by silence and shadow, hiding by turns in shyness, in stillness, in pain, in contemplation, their bodies alternating between states of rest and transmutation. The pain...

events.title: “Abiogenesis” Opening Reception - new works by Philip Beesley & Casey Curran
events.description:
Heron Arts is pleased to announce Abiogenesis, a duo exhibition featuring Philip Beesley and Casey Curran. The opening reception for Abiogenesis is Saturday, November 14th, 2026 from 6-9pm. It is free and open to the public and will be part of San Francisco Art Week. The exhibition will be on view to the public until January 24th, by appointment only.

Abiogenesis brings together the work of Philip Beesley and Casey Curran around an elusive phenomenon: the emergence of life from inert matter. Their work assembles unmistakably artificial elements that, in their cellular forms and gentle movement, begin to suggest life. Lacework becomes membrane. Scaffolds of repeating cells become skeletons of organisms. Glowing, shimmering light evokes the pulses of nature. Mechanical gestures appear to breathe, bloom, and reach into the world.
Intimations of life within Beesley’s and Curran’s sculptures suggest that living form can emerge from the matter of the earth. Beesley and Curran probe this threshold through myth, science, and sensitive sculptural expression.

Artist Bios

Philip Beesley is a Canadian artist whose sculptures explore the threshold between inert matter and living form. At the heart of his work are glowing, pulsing, precious structures composed of innumerable finely crafted elements. Classically trained in fine art and architecture, he creates immersive installations of lace-like scaffolds and suspended membranes, inviting intimate encounters with light, texture, and gen...

Free to attend — RSVP required to reserve your seat.

Speakers
Sara Calvosa Olson (Karuk) is a food writer and editor living in the Bay Area with her husband and two teenage sons. Her work dwells at the intersection of storytelling, Indigenous food systems, security, sovereignty, reconnection, and recipe development. Her writing has appeared in News from Native California and Edible Shasta-Butte. Visit her website at akihsara.com, and follow her on Instagram at @thefrybreadriot.

Chef Crystal Wahpepah, a registered member of the Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma, has long been a warrior for Indigenous food sovereignty. She is the creative tour de force behind the inventive, healthy, and delicious dishes served at her restaurant, Wahpepah’s Kitchen, in Oakland, California—the first Native woman-owned restaurant in Northern California.
If Crystal is not at her Oakland, California restaurant, Wahpepah’s Kitchen, she is on the road, talking about Native American foodways, advocating for Indigenous food sovereignty, and celebrating the launch of her debut cookbook, “A Feather and a Fork.”

Whether he knows it or not, every man lives by a code. And for country provocateur Paul Cauthen, that code is simple. Always bet on yourself. Taught to sing by his grandfather in a Church of Christ, Cauthen hit the scene with the duo Sons of Fathers in 2009, before My Gospel, Room 41, Country Coming Down, and Black on Black unveiled a vulnerable, fire-and-brimstone songwriter with brazen Texas attitude – craving deliverance, yet possessed by a “bird dog” instinct for theatrical rapture. Cauthen has toured the world, collaborating with Margo Price, Orville Peck, Cody Jinks, and Lana Del Rey. Cauthen’s fifth album, Book of Paul, takes him further down his path of utterly authentic country music; fearless, proud, and with two middle fingers in the air. events.description:
The 2026 San Francisco Transgender Film Festival continues with SPECULATIVE FICTION, a shorts block featuring six out of this world films.

Las Cosas Que Brillan (11:09min)

Kristal Sotomayor, United States, 2025

A curious trans mermaid defies her mother’s warnings to venture up to the surface, only to discover the world above is not what she dreamt. Las Cosas Que Brillan explores the impacts of environmental destruction, and the danger of being desired in a postcolonial world.

Motherhood (12:22min)

Ava Corder, United States, 2025

Nicki is one of the first trans women to carry a baby to term as part of a groundbreaking uterine transplant trial. Just hours before her scheduled C-section, her water breaks—something the doctors said couldn’t happen. Her physician urges her to stick to protocol, warning that the outcome of her birth could impact access for future trans patients. Her husband, Benny, and her father, Al, beg her to comply. But Nicki chooses to follow her instinct and pursue a natural birth at home. She’ll give birth on her terms.

Long Away (16:32min)

Tilly Bridges & Susan Bridges, United States, 2025

Set twenty-five years into the future, Long Away is a sci-fi story about Victoria and the father who died when she was very young. As a trans woman who transitioned as an adult, Victoria’s father never got to know her truth. She uses a one-round-trip-only time travel device to jump back to our present and meet the man she can barely remember… and try to find out...

events.title: San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival 2026: Fourth Program
events.description:
The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival returns to the Bay Area to celebrate locally-made cinematic mayhem!

Founded by Peaches Christ & Vinsantos in 2003 at the Bridge Theatre, partially as a showcase for their own short films that weren’t getting traction at “legitimate” festivals, the SFUSFF ran under their care for six years until 2008. After Vinsantos moved to New Orleans, Peaches and fellow film programmer Sam Sharkland wanted to see the fest continue and so revived it in 2011 at the Victoria Theatre where it ran until 2015. Now, after 10 years, the festival has found a new home at the 4 Star Theater under the care of Piranha Psychotronica and Kafka X, the maniacal minds behind Media Meltdown Movie Madhouse.

The San Francisco Underground Short Film Festival exists to celebrate local, independent filmmaking. We proudly champion the overlooked and underrated, the avant-garde and the alternative, the outrageous, the oddball, and the outlandish. We'll be presenting the silly, subversive, surreal, and strange from all Bay Area filmmakers! From bizarro B-films to midnight movie trash, expect the weirdest and wildest the Bay has to offer, with the night kicking off with our lighter fare and getting darker and more freaky as the evening goes on. Cinematic weirdos - you have found the festival for you!

Festival Pass tickets can be selected under any time slot!

events.title: Minnette Lehmann Memorial Celebration
events.description:
Doors 12pm / Program 1pm / Open Mic 2pm

RSVP Here (& register for streaming link)

The Bay Area art community mourns the loss of Minnette Lehmann, feminist artist, intellectual, educator, mother, grandmother, wife, and friend to many, who passed away in June, just shy of her 98th birthday. Minnette was one of the longest-serving board members of The Lab, serving for nearly 20 years.

Please gather with us for a memorial and celebration of Minnette’s extraordinary life, art, sharp wit, dry humor, and indelible legacy. The program will be Emcee’d by Kathy Brew with music by Richard Marriott. Everyone is welcome. (RSVP for a remote online streaming option.)

About Minnette

Since the 1940s, Lehmann was at the forefront of important Bay Area intellectual and artistic movements. She hosted countless artists, thinkers, and art-world gatherings at her San Francisco home and enchanting garden overlooking the Bay.

An embodiment of the “wild woman” archetype, she challenged and redefined domestic and artistic institutions for women, expanding possibilities through photography, performance art, collage, and painting. Her groundbreaking photographic series Trouble in Paradise documented a pivotal moment in American history when marriage itself became problematic. She received a National Endowment for the Arts grant for the work.

events.title: Spotlight Sundays: Japanese American Legacies of Resistance
events.description:
This Sunday, we are stepping into the historical legacy that inspired OMCA’s latest special exhibition, BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration. With opening remarks by OMCA Executive Director Lori Fogarty, we will engage with this present moment in American history with the clarity and learnings of the past.

Guest speakers Satsuki Ina and Miya Sommers, who both have personal or familial ties to wartime incarceration, will be joined in conversation by host Joemy Ito-Gates to explore how the shadows of this history led them to paths of anti-imperialist organizing, solidarity anchored in love, and healing work in times of enduring racial injustice. TaikoPeace will close the day with an interactive performance of “Ei Ja Nai Ka,” honoring Japanese American immigrant ancestors of this era and the echoes of their resistance through taiko, dance, and song. Come ready to learn, engage, and connect with one another!

Visitors are invited to continue the conversation during a post-program Call to Action gathering. Japanese American Families for Justice, Nikkei Resisters, and Tsuru for Solidarity will facilitate interactive protest art activities and share resources on how to get involved with current campaigns.

This program is a part of our exhibition programming for BeHere / 1942: A New Lens on the Japanese American Incarceration, on view through December 27, 2026.

events.title: Paranda Party 3: Jeeti Raho
events.description:
Paranda Party is a queer South Asian cultural celebration built around the paranda, a punjabi hair tassel that is braided into the hair. Now in its third year, this is a night where South Asian culture and queerness share the same room.

This year's theme, Jeeti Raho, takes its name from the blessings our elders give us: jeeti raho, khush raho, abad raho. Stay living, stay happy, stay prosperous. Many of us grew up hearing body-shaming comments in the place those blessings should have been. Jeeti Raho reclaims them, on our own terms.

Join us November 7, 2026 at Queer Arts Featured in the Castro for an evening of live performance, original poetry, and paranda tradition brought to life. Expect original music and spoken word from South Asian and queer artists, a close look at the craft of paranda-making, and a collaborative zine filled with community poetry and artwork, available to take home.

Whether you're returning for your third Paranda Party or walking in for the first time, come ready to celebrate, be loud, and be fully yourself.

events.description:
Presented together, Hunting Flies and Roly Poly are two distinct satirical comedy films by celebrated Director Andrzej Wajda.

Hunting Flies will be preceded by the short film Roly Poly.

Roly Poly – Runtime: 35 minutes

The story of a racing car driver who undergoes so many transplants that it can no longer be determined which people have contributed to his make-up.

Rally driver Richard Fox keeps getting involved in terrible accidents but always manages to survive thanks to organs transplanted from people who died in crashes he caused. The situation complicates when he starts acquiring his donors’ personality traits along with their organs.

Hunting Flies – Runtime: 104 minutes

Wlodek is a shy man who’s afraid of his mother as well as his wife. However, upon meeting Irena, his life takes a new turn.

One of the key films of the Polish film renaissance, this satiric comedy explores the seeming world of emancipated women and emasculated men in Communist Poland. A librarian shares his life and home with his domineering wife. He has an affair with a beautiful intellectual, who wears fly-shaped glasses. She tries to become the woman behind the great artist. It’s a film dedicated to the women of Poland, even as it critiques the relations between the sexes.

Screenings of Andrzej Wajda’s films in the USA in 2026 are part of the ‘Wajda 100 Tour – North America’ project, organized by DI Factory with the financial support of the Polish Film Institute.

events.title: Vince Staples
events.description:
Goldenvoice Presents
Cry Baby Tour
Vince Staples
Sunday, November 15 | The Warfield

It opens with the ephemeral sounds of nature. Birds, bugs, and airy notes chiming in the air. Then, the undercurrent of something darker, disrupting the fantasy: a distorted voice. “To live is to be,” the voice says, “Like the nigga in the tree.” This is how Dark Times, Vince Staples’ eighth studio album, begins.

It’s a new era in the prolific artist’s canon, a muscular and revelatory work refining elements that have been present in his catalog for the last decade: dense lyricism over lush, layered beats; wry, melancholic observations about life; finding pockets of light in an endless dark. For Staples, the album is “a snapshot” of this period of his life.

“It’s been 10 years since I started putting things out properly,” he says, referencing his first EP, with Def Jam in 2014, Shyne Coldchain Vol 2, “I don’t really keep track of any of that stuff, but it’s important to take a second to appreciate the journey.” The title came intuitively to Staples after he listened to the record in full, noticing heavy motifs that kept reappearing. The album cover, featuring a faintly seen noose, was similarly intuitive.

Staples began recording the album over a seven-month stretch, during weekly sessions in North Hollywood. At the time, he was in post-production on his critically acclaimed Netflix series The Vince Staples Show, which he wrote, produced and starred in. Working on the show was “very, very in...

Todd Day Wait is one of the last real American Workhorse, pedal to the metal, Troubadours by way of Missouri, to California, to New Orleans and now Nashville. In an era of excess and endless distraction, the New York-based singer/songwriter Margaret Glaspy rejects the noise in favor of something far more essential. Anna Tivel is a Portland, Oregon-based, internationally touring songwriter who is forever drawn to the quiet stories of ordinary life. The characters and imagery that populate her writing are full of breath and vivid color. With six full-length albums out and a seventh on the way, Anna has been likened to a short story writer and praised by NPR, Rolling Stone, Billboard, and others for her keen observations of the human condition. In fact, Ann Powers of NPR Music had this to say, "Anna Tivel is just one of my absolute favorite living songwriters. George Simon (Hollywood legend John Barrymore, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde) is a successful attorney, climbing from a Jewish ghetto to elegant Art Deco offices in the Empire State Building. It’s no accident that kids everywhere gobble down Lunchables, many of us can’t eat just one Oreo, and warnings by health experts and our own physicians often fail to deter us from loading our shopping carts with ultra-processed foods or pulling up to fast-food restaurants.
The truth is that our cravings for unhealthy foods are the product of extensive research, as well as deliberate manufacturing and marketing decisions, informed by lessons learned by Big Tobacco.
Get the inside skinny on how we’ve been manipulated into eating what makes many of us fat with Laura Schmidt, a highly respected sociologist and public health expert dedicated to understanding how modern lifestyles and economic pressures have driven the rise of chronic disease around the world.
Dr. Schmidt was one of several authors of a recent series of articles in the American Journal of Public Health examining how ultra-processed foods became a huge part of American diets. events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
Distracted AF Tour
Thundercat

Tuesday, November 17 | Fox Theater

We live in a time when our thumbs know more than our minds. We scroll past each other’s joy and grief before breakfast, absorb a day’s worth of tragedy by lunch, and still convince ourselves that the next notification might be the dopamine hit that’ll make us feel better. As much as some of us complain about smartphones — or, more specifically, what’s on said smartphones — distraction is the air we breathe. Social media, surveillance, endless updates and countless opinions, it all piles up until focus feels like a luxury item. For Thundercat, the clutter isn’t abstract. And on Distracted, his long-awaited fifth studio album, it’s the central theme of his life and art right now.

“If you got an Instagram, you know exactly what I’m talking about,” he says matter-of-factly, half joking, half exhausted, when asked the impetus of the album’s title. Thundercat doesn’t frame distraction as a buzzword or a diagnosis; instead, he treats it like something omnipresent, something you deal with whether you like it or not. Distracted arrives six years after 2020’s It Is What It Is, an album shaped by grief, romantic heartbreak, and the sudden loss of his friend and collaborator Mac Miller. If that record felt like a long exhale after trauma, Distracted feels like the restless pacing that follows: the period when life keeps happening whether you’re ready or not. events.title: Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
The Joint Tour
Hamilton Leithauser + Rostam
Wednesday, November 18 | The Castro

At the time I Had a Dream That You Were Mine was first released, the Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam were best known for their work in two of the most influential rock bands of the era: Hamilton as lead singer in The Walkmen and Rostam as the co-songwriter and producer behind Vampire Weekend. The inspired collaboration was born of friendship, and mutual admiration, but grew into a synergistic creative partnership that birthed a timeless album of beautifully evocative songs. I Had a Dream That You Were Mine is a delightfully immersive album, built around Rostam’s meticulous, expansive production and Hamilton’s distinctive, wild vocal range. Unlike anything either artist had done before, the album’s stylistic flourishes include doo-wop, country-rock, baroque pop, folk, and spellbinding torch songs. Together, the lauded musicians found a unique flair for the dramatic which made their handful of live performances a thrilling experience; ten years on, these rare live shows are not to be missed!

Rothmann.
From newspaper dispatches to television broadcasts, radio conversations and news delivered through smartphones, San Francisco’s media have chronicled a city defined by reinvention. Earthquakes, local politics, cultural movements, housing challenges and unforgettable personalities have provided generations of journalists with stories that resonate far beyond the Bay Area.

events.description:
CIIS Public Programs presents renowned mycologist and medical researcher Paul Stamets for an illuminating talk on the history of psilocybin mushrooms exploring their past, present, and future uses. In this presentation, Paul takes you on a journey into the psilocybin mycosphere as he chronicles milestones that further substantiate that psilocybin, and more so psilocybin mushrooms, can help us evolve into the best of what we can be.

The collection and cultivation of psilocybin mushrooms, Paul argues, is central to our practices for freedom of consciousness. Paul shares how psilocybin mushrooms might fundamentally change the many challenges we face as a society. He believes we are at an evolutionary crossroads. Could psilocybin mushrooms help propel us as we emerge into a new version of ourselves, Homo sapiens 3.0?

Paul Stamets, D.Sc. (Honoris causa) is a speaker, author, mycologist, medical researcher, and entrepreneur, who is considered an intellectual and industry leader in fungi. He is the founder and owner of Fungi Perfecti, LLC, and Host Defense Mushrooms supplement line. Paul Stamets is the author of eight books. He named numerous new species of psilocybin mushrooms. In 2023, a new psilocybin mushroom species was named after him to honor his lifelong work: "Psilocybe stametsii." events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Computerwife

New York City-based Addie Warncke began Computerwife in 2018 at the beginning of her college career, using SoundCloud as a diary to chronicle her emotions. When the pandemic hit, Warncke released the five songs she was proudest of as her self-titled debut EP, and the strength of those tracks led to a signing with Danger Collective Records. Now, she’s poised to release her debut self-titled full-length: a raw and intimate portrait of her experiences processing the small but poignant moments that shape a life. Computerwife’s sound is captivating and nuanced, pushing the boundaries between analog and digital. “The main theme that ties this album together is an interest in the deep web and an attempt to combine existing media to make something new,” she explains. With her seamless blend of shoegaze, emo, and lo-fi noise pop, Computerwife speaks directly to the disquiet experienced by every 21st century digital girl with a tenuous grip on life and identity.

Without any prior production knowledge or a band to work with, expanding her songs beyond the writing stage was a challenge Warncke sought to overcome. A Song Exploder episode about Grimes inspired her to download a free trial of Ableton so she could flesh out tracks and learn more about electronic production. On her dorm room bed, she began to record with her dad’s guitar and bass, a Fender deluxe amp, and a focusrite to Ableton. Her first EP and forthcoming debut LP are pulled from thes...

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia
events.description:
Larisa Brechun: Somnia
November 14–December 5

Ryan Graff Contemporary is excited to present Larisa Brechun's debut solo exhibition Somnia.

The subtle qualities of the soul—softness, stillness, fragility, solitude—are often belittled for their “weakness," dismissed as defects of simpering prey in a predatory age, where might and volume rule and humanity fills its hours with chatter and self-exposure. Introspection is the enemy of the social machine, softness a death sentence, silence a grave. And yet, these delicate instincts are essential to the most intimate operation of the soul: the dream.

In Larisa Brechuns’s Somnia, the artist lays bare the quiet privacy of the dreaming mind and the fugitive debris of memory, myth, and imagination as it freely floats in the cocoon of sleep, coalescing into mysterious forms that defy daylight logic. Under her gentle hand, soft animal bodies take shape alongside evaporating cosmic beings and primordial symbols of wilderness, all adrift in the penumbra of the dreaming state, suspended in etheric margins between the deep woodland dark and the flirting light of a winking moon.

Brechun’s darkness has substance, an amplitude of unseen marrow with texture and weight, like a cave or a chrysalis. Lonely figures gently emerge from abyssal thickets, twisting into the light of the omnipresent moon’s awareness as quickly as they recede. They are camouflaged by silence and shadow, hiding by turns in shyness, in stillness, in pain, in contemplation,...

events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Babehoven

Babehoven is the Hudson, NY based project of singer-songwriter Maya Bon and collaborator Ryan Albert. Since 2017, the band has carved out a sound that blends melodic indie and folk rock with an occasional nod towards country. Bon serves as the project’s principal songwriter and lyricist, while Albert, a multi-instrumentalist and producer, further shapes the sonic world around her songs. Together, they’ve built a body of work that feels both intimate and expansive.

"Blue Around You," Babehoven's new single, is a country-flecked stomper. The song finds Bon singing with hard-won resilience: "Yesterday a stranger told me they can see / That I feel levels of pain that could've broken me / And I thought, mmm but I survived it." Recorded at The Chicken Shack and 12 Lb Genius in Upstate NY, Maya and Ryan gathered an excellent crew of musicians with producer Phil Weinrobe at the helm—Oliver Hill, Zosha Warpeha, Dylan Nowik, Jared Samuel, Ellington Peet, and Nick Kinsey. The core of the song was recorded live with no playback or headphones with the feel of the room being as much an instrument as the hardanger fiddle and harmonies that soar overhead.

events.title: Aliens (Special Edition)
events.description:
Where its predecessor was a slow-burn suspenser, Cameron’s ALIENS is a bombastic, no-holds-barred exosuit fight to the finish, an express elevator to hell, goin’ down! Lone survivor Ripley (Sigourney Weaver) goes back for a rematch with the creatures who slaughtered the crew of the Nostromo, this time bringing along a squad of hard-boiled space marines whose number includes the great Bill Paxton, Jenette Goldstein, and Lance Henriksen’s mumblety-peg-playing android Bishop. Rounding out the superb supporting players are the aliens themselves, pinnacles of pre-CGI visual effects that just keep coming, and coming, and coming, and coming… while Mead’s contributions can mostly be seen in the blade-like military vessel Sulaco and the unforgettable “Power Loader” donned by Ripley for the main event grudge match.

Screening in Cameron’s preferred cut, which adds nearly 20 minutes of material not seen in the theatrical version, including glimpses of life at the ill-fated Hadley’s Hope colony and some “kickass” motion-activated turret guns.

“Hot off of the immediate successes of Blade Runner and TRON, Syd Mead was enlisted by Cameron to build out the world of ALIENS, his muscular, action-oriented second chapter to Ridley Scott’s now-iconic 1979 masterpiece. The centerpiece of Mead’s designs is the U.S.S. Sulaco, the military spaceship that transports the Colonial Marines, infusing the vessel with a functional and industrial aesthetic that enhanced the film’s gritty realism.” —Future P...

Her memoir, A Pig in Provence, chronicles her adventures in France, where she still has a home, raising pigs and making goats milk cheese. She lives in Winters, California, with her husband.

events.title: Larisa Brechun: Somnia
events.description:
Larisa Brechun: Somnia
November 14–December 5

Ryan Graff Contemporary is excited to present Larisa Brechun's debut solo exhibition Somnia.

The subtle qualities of the soul—softness, stillness, fragility, solitude—are often belittled for their “weakness," dismissed as defects of simpering prey in a predatory age, where might and volume rule and humanity fills its hours with chatter and self-exposure. Introspection is the enemy of the social machine, softness a death sentence, silence a grave. And yet, these delicate instincts are essential to the most intimate operation of the soul: the dream.

In Larisa Brechuns’s Somnia, the artist lays bare the quiet privacy of the dreaming mind and the fugitive debris of memory, myth, and imagination as it freely floats in the cocoon of sleep, coalescing into mysterious forms that defy daylight logic. Under her gentle hand, soft animal bodies take shape alongside evaporating cosmic beings and primordial symbols of wilderness, all adrift in the penumbra of the dreaming state, suspended in etheric margins between the deep woodland dark and the flirting light of a winking moon.

Brechun’s darkness has substance, an amplitude of unseen marrow with texture and weight, like a cave or a chrysalis. Lonely figures gently emerge from abyssal thickets, twisting into the light of the omnipresent moon’s awareness as quickly as they recede. They are camouflaged by silence and shadow, hiding by turns in shyness, in stillness, in pain, in contemplation,...

events.title: The Lady From Shanghai
events.description:
Baffling murders, fascinating plot twists and remarkable camera work all contribute to this spellbinding, time-honored film noir written, directed by and starring Orson Welles (Citizen Kane, Touch of Evil). Hired to work on a yacht belonging to the disabled husband of femme fatale Rita Hayworth (Gilda, Separate Tables), Welles plays an innocent man drawn into a dangerous web of intrigue and murder. The subject of great controversy and scandal upon its initial release, The Lady from Shanghai shocked 1948 audiences by presenting Hayworth with her flaming red hair cut short and dyed champagne blonde. Decades later, The Lady from Shanghai is considered vintage Welles, his famous hall of mirrors climax hailed as one of the greatest scenes in cinematic history.

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

“As visually striking as it is dramatically effective…subtly exploring the politics of power and control” – Janet Maslin, The New York Times

events.title: Lucy Kaplansky
events.description:
She started out singing in Chicago folk music clubs as a teenager. Then, barely out of high school, Lucy Kaplansky took off for New York City. There she found a fertile community of songwriters and performers—Suzanne Vega, Steve Forbert, The Roches, and others. With a beautiful flair for harmony, Lucy was everyone’s favorite singing partner, but most often she found herself singing as a duo with Shawn Colvin. People envisioned big things for them; in fact, The New York Times said it was “easy to predict stardom for her.” But then Lucy dropped it all.

Convinced that her calling was in another direction, Lucy left the musical fast track to pursue a doctorate in clinical psychology. Upon completing her degree, Dr. Kaplansky took a job at a New York hospital working with chronically mentally ill adults, and also started a private practice. Yet she continued to sing. Lucy was often pulled back into the studio by her friends, (who now had contracts with record labels) wanting her to sing on their albums. She harmonized on Colvin’s Grammy-winning "Steady On," and on Nanci Griffith’s "Lone Star State of Mind" and "Little Love Affairs." She also landed soundtrack credits, singing with Suzanne Vega on "Pretty in Pink" and with Griffith on "The Firm," and several commercial credits as well—including “The Heartbeat of America” for Chevrolet.

events.description:
Brutalismus 3000 are the duo of producer Theo Zeitner and singer Victoria Vassiliki Daldas, two musical visionaries who met on Tinder in 2018 and formed their antagonistic techno band in 2020. With an early hit titled “Satan Was a Babyboomer” and fan-favorite lyrics about “fuckface bouncers,” Brutalismus 3000’s playful attitude and aggressive sound were always too animated for Berlin’s restrictive techno scene. Even so, after rising to fame online during COVID lockdown, the band’s viral songs exploded in European clubs once live music returned, resonating deeply with younger listeners who gleefully reject stodgy genre purism. Since the release of their high-voltage 2023 debut, ULTRAKUNST (LIVE FROM EARTH), Brutalismus 3000 have been mainstays of the international festival circuit -- EDC, Primavera Sound, Coachella, Ultra, Lollapalooza, and more -- and now have friends, fans, and collaborators strewn all across the globe.

For their exhilarating sophomore album, Harmony, Brutalismus 3000 aimed to emphasize their cross-continental influences in a way they never have. The record is a genre-mangling triumph that assembles elements of dubstep, trap, punk, nu-metal, and techno into an eclectic romp of wall-to-wall bangers that includes their most evolved and exciting music yet. Never have Brutalismus 3000 sounded this singular, this sophisticated, this outlandishly absorbing. events.title: Pearl
events.description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.

PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

events.description:
Join WNP Film Club on November 22, 2026 for a screening of a San Francisco noir classic, Dark Passage (1947).

In this atmospheric film, Humphrey Bogart stars as Vincent Parry, a San Francisco man who escapes prison after being wrongly convicted of murdering his wife. With the help of a mysterious woman (Lauren Bacall), he attempts to clear his name while evading the police and searching for the real killer. Filmed on location in San Francisco, Dark Passage blends suspense, romance, and shadowy city streets into a classic noir thriller.

WNP Film Club is a 4 Star Theater series brought to you by Western Neighborhoods Project, your friendly community history nonprofit, in partnership with Bay Area Movies (BAM) and Cinema SF Bay. Join us in celebrating movies filmed on location in San Francisco, with a connection to the west side. This screening will feature an introduction by Jason Moore of BAM and WNP’s resident history nerd, who will share some background about the film and featured locations, including “then and now” comparisons with support from Tim Welsh of SF in Film. Optional Extra Credit: stick around after to unpack the movie with us and indulge your inner film nerd.

The program begins at 7:30 PM on Sunday, November 22. Tickets sales support the 4 Star Theater, BAM and WNP!

Rejected from Cannes for being sacrilegious in its critical depiction of Catholicism’s role in modern Spanish society and marking a major tone shift in Pedro Almodóvar’s filmmaking in the midst of The Movida Madrileña. This piercing psychedelic tale follows cabaret singer Yolanda as she finds refuge in an eccentric convent at risk of financial collapse where the nuns call themselves The Humiliated Redeemers. There, she finds herself among chain-smoking sisters, a pet tiger that can only be soothed by a young Carmen Maura (WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN, VOLVER) playing bongos, and erotic novel smugglers with mustache hairs that blow in the wind. These characters enable each other’s vices and neuroses as they maintain the illusion of seeking salvation under the wing of The Mother Superior, their drug and love addicted leader who uses the mission as a means of luring in needy women. From the deteriorating convent emerges a potent yet playful reminder that we are all sinners that need to be loved.

events.title: Point Blank (1967)
events.description:
British director John Boorman brought a European sensibility to a Los Angeles neo-noir: POINT BLANK is Antonioni plus violence, Francesco Rosi without politics. The title reverberates like a pun-point: blank. Lee Marvin is Walker, left for dead in an Alcatraz heist and now out to find the $93,000 he has coming. No more, no less, unless you count revenge. The trail leads to the City of Angels and the syndicate that runs it out of car lots and Santa Monica penthouses, the kind of places you know exist only with a little larceny. Picking up on the modern surface of his locale, Boorman takes a champagne-blonde color scheme to a hallucinatory degree, blonde on blond, like Angie Dickinson's bouffant and Marvin's silvery pate (here, we have the bad, the brunette, and the bald). Los Angeles is inherently horizontal. The payoff, visually and narratively, occurs in that storm drain affectionately known as the L.A. River, viewed from a bridge over imagined waters. (BAMPFA)

DCP courtesy of Warner Bros.

On this world tour, the new songs will be presented alongside the old favorites that have stayed with listeners all these years. Between 2017 and 2018, Song Dongye released three pivotal singles—“Empty Harbor Song,” “Guo Yuan Chao,” and “To Know”—each quietly expanding the boundaries of folk music and reshaping the industry’s perception of him. Now, thirteen years after his landmark debut Anhe Bridge North, arrives his long-awaited second album, Take Another Moment. Entirely self-conceived, arranged, and produced, it stands as a work that, even now, surpasses all expectations upon listening. Over the years, he has lost weight. He fishes. He takes photographs. He plays with beads. And he has completed Take Another Moment, an album astonishing in both its lyrical scope and sonic depth. He remains the songwriter, arranger, and producer at the center of his work. Alongside him are more than twenty instruments and sound sources, leading lights of China’s jazz world such as Wen Zhiyong, Xia Jia, and Nathaniel Gao, and independent spirits as subtle and reclusive as Xing Jiangbo He is still occasionally playful, perhaps as a way of balancing his absolute seriousness and devotion to music—once even letting his cat's backside appear on an album cover. Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

events.title: The Cook, The Thief, His Wife, & Her Lover
events.description:
Peter Greenaway's 1989 magnum opus THE COOK, THE THIEF, HIS WIFE & HER LOVER is neo-noir for the hungry, devious soul. Released at a time when crime cinema was growing increasingly perverse with the likes of ANGEL HEART (1987), BLUE VELVET (1986), and BODY DOUBLE (1984), Greenaway's film out-shocks the buch by intertwining two of human nature's favorite pastimes: food and sex. Like Marco Ferreri's LA GRAND BOUFFE (1973) and Paul Bartel's EATING RAOUL (1982) before it, food and sex quickly turn into a recipe for something decidedly more sinister and... cannibalistic. Shocking audiences at the time of its release, time has not tamed Greenaway's film at all, and you'll never look at Helen Mirren or Michael Gambon the same way again. (Justin LaLiberty)

In a castle in the San Fernando Valley lies the lair of music icon Gary Numan. Outside is an enormous statue of a dragon, inside a St Bernard (almost as large) greets you on arrival. Notorious for hits such as 'Are 'Friends' Electric?' and 'Cars', Numan's early career was too often misconstrued, tainted by a sometimes fraught relationship with the media and challenged by the hostility of the music industry at the time, still deeply committed as it was to the guitar, bass, drums approach of old. Numan, however, stuck to his guns, outlasted his naysayers, and became renowned not just as a pioneer but as an institution. Today, with a career that has spanned nearly four decades, his approach to electronic music remains an inspiration to artists across genres and eras, from stadium goliaths such as Depeche Mode, Prince and Nine Inch Nails to alternative heroes such as Beck, Damon Albarn and Marilyn Manson. Even Kanye West owes him a debt and David Bowie once credited him with ‘writing two of the finest songs’ in British music. It's no surprise he recently received the Ivor Novello Award for Inspiration.

Now, Numan is preparing his 22nd studio album titled ' Savage (Songs From A Broken World)'. He's a busy guy. A self-proclaimed “one man band”, Numan has always been something of an outlier living on his own terms....

The Wrecks are nothing if not resourceful.

The group’s very origin story is a testament to a rare level of D.I.Y. craftiness that has quietly cemented them as an independent phenomenon with an intensely faithful fan base, over a quarter-of-a-billion streams, and successive sold-out headline tours.

Rewinding back to the beginning, the Los Angeles-based band— Nick Anderson [vocals, guitar, keyboard, production], Nicholas “Schmizz” Schmidt [lead guitar], Aaron Kelley [bass], and William “Billy” Nally [drums]—actually recorded their first batch of tunes under clandestine cover in a “borrowed studio.”

Leaving a small town in New York, Nick had just moved to Los Angeles with a handful of songs. He wound up teaching them to his new bandmates and recording them in the evening at a professional studio in the backyard of a home where his friend was house-sitting.

Everything went according to plan until the last night

“We worked from 5pm until 9am for three days,” he recalls. “On the final day, the girl called us and said, ‘You’ve got to get out of there. The owner is on the way’. We cleaned up, grabbed our gear, and left. As we were pulling out, this woman pulled into the driveway. However, we forgot to dump our work onto an external,” he laughs. “Our buddy snuck back in at 2am, stayed in the dark, and transferred the songs. Expect to relive all of their favorites, including “We’ve Only Just Begun”, “Close to You”, and “Rainy Days and Mondays” with this heartfelt love letter to the quiet magic of Karen and Richard Carpenter.

events.title: MC5: A True Testimonial
events.description:
CHUCK PROPHET’S CINEMA DISCOTHEQUE presents:

MC5: A TRUE TESTIMONIAL

This documentary, made over a period of eight years, tells the remarkable story of an extremely influential rock’n’roll band. Starting from their mid-60’s garage band roots (sounding amazingly like the Sonics), the Motor City 5 deveoped into an icon for a brand of loud, crushing music reflecting their industrial roots. Even if you don’t care for their music (and you’re bound to like even a few of their songs), their story is fascinating. It combines 60’s protest, youthful braggadocio, and a style of music that would help carry one to the likes of Iggy and the Stooges (not to mention certain aspects of punk rock). This film is clearly a labor of love, combining extraordinarily rare live shows, still shots, a nearly-continuous backdrop of MC5 tunes, penetrating interviews with the remaining members and their spouses, and even FBI surveillance shots. It’s the ultimate testimonial to a band that only gains in stature as time goes on.

DOORS at 7:00 PM | FILM at 7:30 PM

events.title: Amtrac
events.description:
Long established for his chameleonic proficiency, Amtrac spent the last decade proving himself with melodic house tracks, infectious indie dance hooks and everything in between. Amtrac is a multi-instrumentalist, vocalist, producer, and DJ. He’s played sold-out arena shows, underground clubs and festivals around the world. His recent co-headline tour with Tourist sold out venues across North America.

He’s released three full-length albums and a slew of varied singles and EPs, not to mention marquee collaborations with Diplo and Leon Bridges, Elderbrook, Shakka and Kaskade. He’s remixed everyone from Bob Moses to Alesso, Two Door Cinema Club, Ellie Goulding, Washed Out, UNKLE, Axwell/Ingrosso, ZHU, Bob Moses & more. He runs his own label, Openers, named in a nod to the way he’s managed to straddle both the bright lights of the mainstage world and the taste-making underground without ever losing sense of who he really is—and still, he’s never felt quite as focused as this.

events.title: The Music of Hey Arnold! Live Ft. Jim Lang and the PS 118 AllStars
events.address: 417 Alvarado Street, Monterey, CA, Monterey, CA, 93940
events.description:
The Music of Hey Arnold! Live featuring Jim Lang & The PS 118 AllStars celebrates the 30th anniversary of one of television's most cherished animated series.

Led by award winning composer Jim Lang, best known for his unforgettable theme music, original songs, and score for Hey Arnold!, this one of a kind concert brings the music of the series to life on stage. Blending jazz, hip hop, blues, R&B and funk, Lang created a sound unlike anything else on television, helping give Hey Arnold! its heart, warmth, humor and soul. Thirty years later, the music continues to connect with fans of all ages and inspire musicians around the world.

Performed by Jim Lang and The PS 118 AllStars, the evening features the show's unforgettable themes, fan favorite songs, and some of the moments that made Hey Arnold! so special. Accompanied by multimedia visuals and stories from behind the music, the performance also includes a special guest appearance by series creator Craig Bartlett.

Whether you grew up with Hey Arnold! or are discovering its music for the first time, this 30th anniversary celebration is a chance to experience one of animation's most distinctive and enduring scores performed live by the composer who created it.

events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Djuna Devereaux and Rolf Gates
When stress and uncertainty arise, returning to the body and our connection with the earth offers stability, calm, and the possibility of a wise response. In this daylong retreat, we’ll cultivate embodied presence as a taproot—grounding us and settling the mind. From this refuge, we’ll explore opening to clarity, joy, and belonging.
Our day will weave together Dharma teachings, meditation, somatic movement, and yoga asana into a deeply nourishing experience. We’ll begin with floor-based movement to release tension and fatigue, then flow into accessible yoga sequences. Drawing on personal stories and classical Buddhist teachings, we’ll explore what it means to be grounded in the body, held by awareness, and supported by community. All abilities and levels of experience warmly welcomed!

events.title: Zhang Yimou’s Raise the Red Lantern (4K Restoration)
events.description:
Co-presented by Bay Area Chinese Culture Salon and Amoment Books.

Nineteen-year-old Songlian, a promising student whose family has been destroyed by her father’s death, is forced to abandon her studies and marry into wealth, becoming the fourth and newest concubine of the aging, unseen Master Chen. Inside his walled estate, she discovers a household ruled by a merciless ritual: each night, red lanterns are lit outside the chambers of whichever wife the master chooses to visit, granting her privilege and status while the others are cast into cold irrelevance. Songlian is drawn into the orbit of her rivals, each shaped by years of fighting for the same scraps of attention. Determined at first to rise above the games, Songlian is gradually worn down by isolation and humiliation until she strikes back, trading secrets and favors to secure her place in Master Chen’s hierarchy. As petty cruelty turns even more dire, Songlian is forced to confront what these desperate measures will cost her soul.

One of international cinema’s greatest stars of the era, Gong Li is “nuanced and understated” (Chicago Reader) as the stifled young woman forced into a repressive world of concubinage. Newly restored, the film stands as one of the defining works of Fifth Generation Chinese cinema and international film of the 1990s.

events.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown (35mm)
events.description:
This fast-paced celebration of hysteria put Almodóvar on the map by joyfully parading his depthless obsession with women – especially the wild ones. Driven to the brink by her married lover, Pepa (Carmen Maura) cries at work, lights her bed on fire, and loads the gazpacho with barbiturates. Her girlfriends don’t fare much better in this melodramatic farce that runs at a constant parody-level soap-operatic pitch. It’s no small coincidence that during filming Carmen Maura grew so angry with the director she outright refused to speak to him. Men drive the women of this movie to crisis – a trash collector, Shiite terrorists, boyfriends, Antonio Banderas – and the women fight back as a series of peculiar coincidences tightens the social fabric of Madrid. “I thought this only happened in the movies,” a cab driver tells Pepa after she has him tail another cab. Yeah yeah, her expression says, but it’s headed somewhere very interesting.

events.title: Indigenous Voices: Joey Clift and Terria Smith in conversation
events.description:
Join us as we close out our Native American Heritage Month series, welcoming Joey Clift and Terria Smith to share their latest works — We've Been Here The Whole Time! and I Love You So Many.

Free to attend — RSVP required to reserve your seat.

Speakers
Joey Clift is a Los Angeles-based, Peabody and 2x Emmy Award-nominated comedian, writer, director, producer and enrolled member of the Cowlitz Indian Tribe.
Joey attended college to become a local TV weather person because as a kid he didn’t see any Native American comedians on television, and that made him believe he wasn’t allowed to work in comedy. Since then he has learned that this is not true – and his comedy style reflects that. Joey’s work has been featured in The Washington Post, Pitchfork, NPR, Dead Meat, Dropout and Comedy Central.

Terria Smith is a tribal member of the Torres Martinez Desert Cahuilla Indians and a proud original Californian. She is the editor of News from Native California magazine and director of the Berkeley Roundhouse, Heyday’s California Indian publishing program. Smith is also the editor of the 2023 anthology Know We Are Here: Voices of Native California Resistance. She received her undergraduate degree at Cal Poly Humboldt (formerly Humboldt State University) and earned her master’s degree at the UC Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism. She lives on her ancestral homelands in the Coachella Valley with her puppy Havana.

events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
For 58 years, Tower of Power has delivered the best in funk and soul music. East Bay Grease defined their sound and landed them with Warner Brothers. Bump City, their 1972 debut for the label, was a hit on both the Billboard 200 and the R&B Albums. The 70s were a boom period with radio classics like “So Very Hard to Go” and “What Is Hip,” and the band continued to tour and record over the years. Fifty years later, in 2018, they returned to Oakland to celebrate their landmark 50th anniversary. Tower’s window-rattling grooves and raucous party spirit had been a balm for the soul throughout their half-century existence.

The band has traveled the world, enjoying hit singles on their own and backing legendary artists, including Otis Redding, Elton John, Santana, the Grateful Dead, John Lee Hooker, Aerosmith, Bonnie Raitt, and countless others. In the process they’ve defined an “Oakland soul” sound as instantly recognizable as those from Castillo’s hometown, Detroit, as well as inspirations like Memphis and Philadelphia.

Stay Out is a high-energy punk rock band from Oakland, California, rooted deep in the East Bay DIY scene and driven by a relentless commitment to authenticity, connection, and explosive live performance. The lineup was solidified in 2018 with the addition of drummer Nate Reynoso, whose impact on the band’s songwriting and sound helped push their evolution into something sharper, louder, and more cohesive.

Drawing from the legacy of Bay Area punk while carving out their own lane, Stay Out fuses high-octane punk rock with pop-punk accessibility, creating music that’s both chaotic and emotionally resonant. Their lyrics tap into themes of defiance, isolation, struggle, and social tension—reflecting real experiences while maintaining an undercurrent of resilience and unity. events.title: New People: An Eye for an Eye
events.description:
This screening will take place at NEW PEOPLE CINEMA, located at 1746 Post Street in Japantown.

Director Tanaz Eshaghian in person for a post-screening Q&A

An Eye for an Eye unfolds like a real-life courtroom thriller, with stakes as high as life and death. Years after killing her abusive husband in an act of self-defense, Tahereh now faces execution unless she can pay the Diya—blood money demanded by her abuser’s family. With the clock ticking and public sympathy running low, her son Mohsen is thrust into a desperate race against time to save his mother’s life, turning to outside donors in a society where victims of domestic abuse are often met with silence—or scorn. With unprecedented access to private negotiations, legal proceedings, and intimate family moments, the filmmakers bring us deep inside a harrowing moral and legal labyrinth. We witness not only the emotional toll on Tahereh and her children, but also the chilling mechanics of a justice system shaped by patriarchal values and religious law. Gripping and deeply human, An Eye for an Eye lays bare the personal costs of systemic injustice—and the fierce resilience of a family fighting for their right to move forward.

As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. TRASH & TREASURES presents:

BEGOTTEN

When it debuted in 1989, E. Elias Merhige’s Begotten fascinated and shocked those who witnessed it. Never before had the screen depicted such a primal, existential drama, and it became one of the must-see films of the 1990s. The intervening decades have not diminished the power of this unique motion picture experience. This new 4K restoration reveals the full photographic body of Begotten, preserving its otherworldly organic texture and retaining its visceral impact, a previously unknown life form captured in cinematic amber.

events.title: Small Town Gay Bar
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment Presents
20th Anniversary
Small Town Gay Bar
Hosted by Peaches Christ w/ special guest Director Malcolm Ingram
Tuesday, December 1 | The Castro

Two decades ago, director Malcolm Ingram shined a beautiful, raw, and deeply moving spotlight on the resilience of LGBTQ+ communities in the Deep South with his groundbreaking documentary, Small Town Gay Bar. This year, we are bringing it back to San Francisco’s most iconic silver screen.

Small Town Gay Bar is a tribute to the resiliency of gays living in rural areas throughout America. A moving portrait of men and women fighting to create and maintain community for themselves in the face of great opposition, hypocrisy and prejudice in a largely ignored subculture of discreet backdoor entrances and hushed sexual expression in small town Mississippi.

Experience the film like never before with a gorgeous, brand-new 4K restoration print that captures every ounce of heart, struggle, and triumph in crystal-clear definition. Following the screening, Peaches will sit down with special guest director Malcolm Ingram for an exclusive, live Q&A diving deep into the legacy of the film, behind-the-scenes secrets, and how the landscape of queer safe spaces has evolved over the last twenty years.

Don’t miss this rare opportunity to celebrate queer history, cinema, and community at the Castro Theatre!

Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
Directed by Paul Thomas Anderson
Presented in 35mm

Wednesday, December 2 | The Castro

Cameron Winter, in December 2025, after a months-long sold-out tour with his band Geese, returned to New York to play a single show at Carnegie Hall. This is the movie.

Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Oscar-winning filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson (One Battle After Another), the crew includes filmmaker and actor Benny Safdie (The Smashing Machine) and music producer Ariel Rechtshaid (Grammy winner for albums with Vampire Weekend and Adele).

GQ praised Cameron Winter’s show at Carnegie Hall as “staggeringly good,” and Nick Cave said he has a “a glorious, emotive voice with brilliant, blistering words, a racked and wondrous thing.” Winter’s solo album Heavy Metal was named one of the best of the year by Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, Paste and Mojo and Geese’s last record Getting Killed was named the best album of 2025 by The New Yorker, NME, and Stereogum.

Directed and choreographed by Tony and Olivier Award-nominated Jennifer Weber, this contemporary dance spectacle is a re-mixed and re-imagined version of the classic, smashing hip hop dance and Tchaikovsky’s timeless music together into a heart-stirring and inspirational holiday event. The Hip Hop Nutcracker is brought to life by a powerhouse cast of a dozen all-star dancers, a DJ, a violinist, and MC Kurtis Blow, one of hip hop’s founding fathers, who opens the show with a short set.

Just like the original, in The Hip Hop Nutcracker, Maria-Clara and the Nutcracker Prince go on a dream adventure battling a gang of mice, visiting the land of sweets and learning the lessons of the holiday season. Innovative digital graffiti and visuals transform the landscape of E.T.A. Hoffmann’s beloved story from traditional 19th Century Germany to the vibrant, diverse sights and sounds of contemporary New York City.

Grab your family and friends and let the dynamic performers of The Hip Hop Nutcracker take you on a journey that celebrates love, community and the magic of the holiday season.

Christmas movies come and go, but few join the pantheon of the greats. You know the ones – A CHRISTMAS STORY, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE, and MIRACLE ON 34TH STREET.
