events.title: Angels in America, Part One: Millennium Approaches
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPhoto by Crystal LiuIn the first part of Tony Kushner’s Pulitzer-winning epic, set in 1980’s New York City, a gay man is abandoned by his lover when he contracts the AIDS virus, and a closeted Mormon lawyer’s marriage to his pill-popping wife stalls. Other characters include the infamous McCarthy-ite lawyer Roy Cohn, Ethel Rosenberg, a former drag queen who works as a nurse, and an angel.
Between its 1993 Broadway premiere and its 2017 National Theatre revival, Angels’ mythical status has expanded, onstage and off. But to director and actor John Fisher, this play is best experienced when presented up close, with its human heartbreaks and joys mere feet from the audience. “[Theatre Rhinoceros] is ‘IMAX’ theatre – it’s immediate, it’s right there, you could touch the actors. It’s always been staged as an epic, as opposed to a lived experience. And I don’t believe it was written as an epic, it was written as a ‘fantasia’ – and fantasy is immersive, not witnessed.”

The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.

events.title: Haiku in the Garden – Autumn
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerMarin Art and Garden CenterJoin us to savor the poetry of the season, in this free gathering hosted by Jayne McPherson.
Gardens have an essential and ubiquitous place in lyric poetry. The great poet Kahlil Gibran called friendship a garden, one where planted seeds are sown “with love and reap thanksgiving.”

During this season, let’s follow his poetic lead and look up at distant mountains that frame the lazy lady on the horizon. Let’s remind ourselves of the middle pond’s pink and white lotus blossoms-that they float night and day under the sun or moonlight. Let’s notice how the water fountain’s splash undulates in ringlets; how, inside the iron gate, blossoms protrude as promises kept in heirloom roses; how a giving-tree oak allows another woodpecker or squirrel to sneak substance and nest.
Haiku offers beauty in form and empathy. And like a harvest, it can evoke awe or perhaps simply ahhh. When we seek pause in the natural world, we may remember our breath and breathe more deeply. We may tune in, feel our heartbeat, sense a door opening as we pause before a sunning lizard or grazing deer.
Writing haiku is a quiet way to savor these Garden gifts.
This is our third anniversary writing circle and will feature haikuist, David Watts. His poetry has been published widely. It includes two books, Dream Tree & Seed Kites.
David Watts is recognized by Haiku Poets of Northern California.
For all ages, this simple yet focused writing has benefits beyond...

Featured photo by Sachi CunninghamHeavy Water Collective Presents: Ocean Beach brings together 24 photographers who turn their lenses toward the Pacific, finding pockets of magic amidst a vast liquid field of chaos.

Others ask you to forget the city and immerse in how light, energy, and human shapes can dance together. Each photograph displays a single permutation within an infinite, ever-changing landscape.

events.title: ZooLights at San Francisco Zoo (Nov. 6-Jan 3)
events.description:
San Francisco Zoo & GardensSan Francisco Zoo & Gardens is thrilled to announce its all-new, two-month-long ZooLights evening holiday program that will light up the Zoo in spectacular fashion from November 6 through January 3, 2027. The nighttime event represents the return of ZooLights, which the Zoo last hosted in 2018.

“The Zoo is the perfect venue for a safe, outdoor holiday lights experience,” said Cassandra Costello, CEO and Executive Director. “We have taken this event to the next level, creating 14 dazzling zones, with winter, botanical or animal-themed components. It’s going to be truly breathtaking, and a great experience for the entire family.”

In addition to traditional holiday zones, where guests will walk through awe-inspiring lighted tunnels and stroll among giant candy canes, giant ornaments and gift boxes, there’s an entire frozen zone, with 10-foot-tall icicles, sparkling snowflakes, a frozen forest, a massive ice throne and frozen sleigh for that perfect family photo.

“The effect will be magical,” said Costello. “Overall, ZooLights will have more than one million lights, and the walk-through areas include amazing photo ops, and nods to the City of San Francisco with a Golden Gate Bridge and the iconic cable car.”

Whimsical animal shapes and scenes will dot the landscape, using 2D and 3D illuminations of a rhino and gorilla, even a tree full of ring-tailed lemurs. Vibrantly colored, larger-than-life butterflies are part of an enchanting botanical pathway,...

In this rollicking autobiographical comedy, Janet moves from Colorado to San Francisco in 1972, where a closed-head injury, late-in-life love, even-later-in-life parenthood, and a divorce await her, along with a right-wing coup led by one of the seven subpersonalities in her psyche. Wild Child, Rosie, and Mauve love San Francisco; Raisin and Hannah want to go home. Cora soothes Raisin with cinnamon rolls while Hannah frets about sugar. Hannah and Wild Child clash over partying. Rosie wants new clothes and skin care; Mauve wants writers’ conferences. Add the shock of becoming an elder, and something has got to give.

From the producers of Memoir comes a unique new theatrical circus experience.

In/Decision is an exploration of the moments that define us, the leaps we take, the risks we avoid, the paths we choose without knowing where they lead. Through a seamless weaving of breathtaking aerials, acrobatics and storytelling, this original production invites audiences into the fragile space between choice and consequence.
Each act balances on the edge of possibility: releasing the bar, shifting weight, moving forward, or taking a step back. A character speaks, or stays silent. In these suspended moments, worlds are made and unmade.
Poetic, visceral, and deeply human, In/Decision asks: Are we guided by destiny, or do we build it step by step?
Come join us, and decide.
Doors open one hour before the show starts.

events.venue: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art (SFMOMA)
events.description:
Manilatown Heritage Foundation“Two Films. One Manilatown Legacy.” brings two generations of San Francisco’s Manilatown and International Hotel history to the big screen at SFMOMA for a special FREE double-feature presentation.
At 1 PM, experience the San Francisco premiere of the newly enhanced and restored edition of Curtis Choy’s landmark 1983 documentary, “The Fall of the I-Hotel”. The film chronicles the decade-long struggle to save San Francisco’s International Hotel and the August 4, 1977 eviction of its predominantly Filipino and Chinese elder tenants. Following the screening, filmmaker Curtis Choy joins co-producers of the enhanced edition for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.
At 3 PM, experience the premiere of “Manilatown Manang”, the story of Jeanette Gandionco Lazam-artist, activist, and one of the few women who lived in the International Hotel as a Tenant Defender during the historic anti-eviction movement. The film follows Jeanette’s journey from the I-Hotel struggle through a lifetime of activism, art, and community. Following the premiere, Jeanette Lazam joins the film’s producers and creative team for a community conversation moderated by Caroline Ocampo.

Together, the films create a powerful dialogue between past and present: audiences first encounter Jeanette as a young activist in Choy’s historic documentary, then experience the continuation of her story in Manilatown Manang.

events.title: Free “Wood Street” Film Screening on Oakland’s Unhoused + Q&A (SF Main Library)
events.description:
Caron CreightonWOOD STREET follows a year in the life of Oakland’s largest unhoused encampment as its residents face an imminent eviction that threatens to dismantle their community. As notices appear and police move in, residents organize — building barricades, filing lawsuits, and protesting at City Hall to fight for their right to stay. Told through immersive verité, the film places viewers inside the encampment, capturing the urgency, resilience, and emotional toll of collective resistance. At its center are John and LaMonté, whose bond is tested as pressure mounts — LaMonté’s mental health deteriorates while John struggles to remain sober. When the eviction comes, the community is physically erased, but its spirit endures.
The film will be followed by a Q&A with the film team, members of the Wood Street community and the editor of Street Sheet newspaper.

events.title: Free Night Walking Tour of Chinatown Alleyways + North Beach
events.address: Bush Street &, Grant Ave, San Francisco, CA 94108
events.description:
Filip ToddAfter dark, Chinatown quiets down. That’s when this walk starts.
It’s a free 90-minute evening tour that begins at the Dragon Gate and works up through Chinatown’s back alleys to the point where the neighbourhood turns into North Beach. Along the way: the old tong buildings on Waverly Place, the gambling alleyways, a Bruce Lee mural, Jack Kerouac Alley and City Lights Bookstore. It ends at Golden Boy Pizza.
Two neighbourhoods pressed up against each other for more than a century, and the seam between them is the most interesting part of either.

The tour is free in the real sense — no ticket, nothing paid up front. At the end you decide what it was worth, and there’s no obligation.
Guided in English. Meets at the Dragon Gate, corner of Bush Street and Grant Avenue.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCaleb Dardick, authorIn 1970, five-year-old Caleb Dardick set off with his family on an extraordinary 20,000-mile journey from Amsterdam to India in a VW bus. His father used a wheelchair, his mother was living with undiagnosed bipolar disorder, and the three children found themselves immersed in the counterculture’s wild search for freedom and enlightenment.
Join Dardick at San Francisco’s Adobe Books for a free reading and discussion of his new memoir, The Adventures of Superfreak: My Childhood on the Hippie Trail (Running Wild Press, 2026).

The book is a child’s-eye view of the counterculture, filled with adventure, humor, wonder, and instability. As San Francisco approaches the 60th anniversary of the Summer of Love in 2027, Dardick offers an unusual perspective on that era: the children who were along for the ride.
A former San Francisco resident who spent nearly three decades in Berkeley, Dardick wrote much of the memoir in the Bay Area.

Adobe Books, 3130 24th Street, San Francisco
Free admission. No RSVP required. Books available for purchase and signing.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerFred BrillYou don’t want to miss the November 10 Conundrum Chronicles StorySlam! (The Marsh Theater– 1062 Valencia Street, SF)
Put your name in the hat for a chance to tell a true five-minute story; be the judge; or kick back and enjoy magic of live storytelling!

Others are quiet: a sentence someone said, a choice you almost didn’t make, a morning that looked like any other morning until it wasn’t. Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerDennis BoltCan Music Change the Course of History?
Three centuries ago, George Frideric Handel explored a bold idea: that music can change how people think, feel, and act.

Music Director Peter Whelan and Philharmonia Baroque Orchestra & Chorale open the 2026/27 season with Handel’s The Power of Music, featuring Alexander’s Feast, a vocal and choral masterpiece inspired by a legendary banquet marking Alexander the Great’s victory over Persia. As the feast unfolds, poet-musician Timotheus uses music to influence the conqueror and change the course of history.
Bay Area audiences will be first in the U.S. to hear Handel’s 1742 Dublin version, performed on period instruments and in the style of the time.

events.title: 29th Anniversary San Francisco Transgender Film Festival (Nov. 12-14)
events.description:
San Francisco Trans Film FestivalNovember 12-14, screenings at 7pm-8pm and 9pm-10pm each night\
Sliding scale tickets for screenings start at $5 (plus $1.28 fee)
The San Francisco Transgender Film Festival (SFTFF) celebrates 29 years of innovative, experimental, and outside-the-box films by transgender and gender-nonconforming filmmakers.

Spanning 12-days from November 12-22 and comprised of seven short film programs showcasing 37 films, SFTFF 2026 will be a hybrid festival, presented both in person and online, and featuring a range of genres from documentaries and politics to animation, dance, music, romance, coming-of-age tales, and thrillers.
SFTFF will host in-person programs Nov. 12-14 at the Roxie Theater, 3117 16th St., SF and will offer on demand access to each of the programs through Nov. 22nd. Films are closed captioned for Deaf and hard-of-hearing audiences; tickets are $0-$50, sliding scale/donation-based, inclusive of fees.
Presented by San Francisco Trans Film Festival

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Echoes of the Seasons: A Piano Dialogue Between East and West
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLExplore how Eastern and Western composers interpret the seasons across different musical traditions. Western selections express vivid natural imagery, from Vivaldi’s dynamic storms to Tchaikovsky’s romantic winter scenes and the reflective mood of Autumn Leaves. These works translate the physical world into sound through color, emotion and narrative.
Eastern musical philosophy centers Yijing (意境), an aesthetic that blends atmosphere, poetry and spiritual resonance. Rooted in the Chinese pentatonic scale, this approach moves beyond direct depiction, inviting listeners to experience nature as a contemplative reflection of the self.

Through classical masterworks, jazz and traditional Chinese repertoire, this lecture‑recital highlights how artistic languages encounter one another across cultures. The program invites audiences to hear how different musical philosophies interpret the seasons and how these perspectives generate deeper understanding of memory, place and expression.

events.title: Fort Point Beer Co Presents: Manzanita Night
events.description:
Fort Point Beer Co

A one-night celebration at Fort Point Valencia to honor our favorite fall tradition: the release of our Manzanita Smoked Altbier.

Join us as we kick off Manzanita season with a night we hope becomes an annual tradition. The cask taps at 5:30pm. Be there for the toast and first pour.
Brewed with charred local manzanita branches, Manzanita is a beautiful dark beer that’s light-bodied and somehow nutty, herbal, sweet and savory all at once. Decisively autumnal without relying on the clichés of the season, it’s our very Northern California take on the classic smoked beers of Northern Bavaria and a Fort Point cult favorite.

Cask-conditioned Manzanita: Gravity-poured from a cask on the bar, the way they still serve it in Bamberg, the world’s smoked beer capital. Get it before the cask runs dry.
Smoked beer flights: Manzanita (cask & draft) alongside selections from Bamberg’s historic Schlenkerla and Freigeist, the experimental brewery that we collabed with on the very first Manzanita batch.
Manzanita steins: Rastal ceramic half liters, custom printed with the Manzanita icon. Fill one at the bar and take it home. Limited run, while supplies last.
First 4-packs of the season: Sold to go before they’re available anywhere else.

events.title: Free 2026 Art Week Opening: Kinetic Sculpture Show “Abiogenesis” at SF’s Heron Arts
events.description:
Image courtesy of artists.Heron Arts is pleased to announce Abiogenesis, a duo exhibition featuring Philip Beesley and Casey Curran. The opening reception for Abiogenesis is Saturday, November 14th, 2026 from 6-9pm. It is free and open to the public and will be part of San Francisco Art Week. The exhibition will be on view to the public until January 24th, by appointment only.

Abiogenesis brings together the work of Philip Beesley and Casey Curran around an elusive phenomenon: the emergence of life from inert matter. Their work assembles unmistakably artificial elements that, in their cellular forms and gentle movement, begin to suggest life. Lacework becomes membrane. Scaffolds of repeating cells become skeletons of organisms. Glowing, shimmering light evokes the pulses of nature. Mechanical gestures appear to breathe, bloom, and reach into the world.

Intimations of life within Beesley’s and Curran’s sculptures suggest that living form can emerge from the matter of the earth. Beesley and Curran probe this threshold through myth, science, and sensitive sculptural expression.

Artist Bios

Philip Beesley is a Canadian artist whose sculptures explore the threshold between inert matter and living form. At the heart of his work are glowing, pulsing, precious structures composed of innumerable finely crafted elements. Classically trained in fine art and architecture, he creates immersive installations of lace-like scaffolds and suspended membranes, inviting intimate encounters w...

events.title: Free Astronomy Talk: Chile’s Giant Observatories (Randall Museum)
events.description:
The San Francisco Amateur Astronomers invite you to this free public event.
Chile is home to many of the largest and most advanced observatories on Earth, due to high altitudes, dry deserts, and low light pollution. Chile has become a center of cutting edge astronomical research, but this has been made possible by the collaborative efforts of multiple countries and the work of scientists and engineers from around the globe. This past summer I had the opportunity to participate in the Astronomy in Chile Educator Ambassadors Program (ACEAP). The program took me to the major observatories (ALMA, Vera Rubin, Gemini South, and more) and met many of the people who keep the observatories running. I’ll be sharing my insights into Chile, international astronomical collaborations, and the southern skies.
Brian “Astro” Castro is an amateur astronomer in San Francisco known for his pop-up sidewalk astronomy events in The Mission, around SF, and occasionally around the world. From 4” travel scopes that fit in a carry-on with room to spare, to 16” Dobsonians, he has shown the cosmos to over 15,000 people. He has organized for the local chapter of The Planetary Society, solo traveled to Guatemala to personally donate telescopes to schools and instruct in their use, and even strapped a large telescope to a bicycle trailer and biked around showing Saturn to festival goers at Burning Man in the Black Rock Desert. He is a 2025 ACEAP Ambassador

On Thursday, November 19, Heather Knight, San Francisco bureau chief for The New York Times, will moderate a panel featuring Will Hearst, editor and publisher of Alta Journal; award-winning television journalist Wendy Tokuda; political reporter Joe Fitzgerald Rodriguez of The San Francisco Standard; and radio host and political commentator John F. Rothmann.

From newspaper dispatches to television broadcasts, radio conversations and news delivered through smartphones, San Francisco’s media have chronicled a city defined by reinvention. Earthquakes, local politics, cultural movements, housing challenges and unforgettable personalities have provided generations of journalists with stories that resonate far beyond the Bay Area.
Bringing together perspectives from print, television, digital news and radio, the evening will explore how the city’s stories reach audiences, how journalism has changed and what endures as new technologies reshape the media landscape. events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

LBFE-SFJoin us this Thanksgiving as we bring warmth, joy, and holiday meals to older adults in our community! There are two ways you can volunteer:
Option 1: In-Person Visit & Meal Delivery

Pick up your Thanksgiving meal(s) in downtown San Francisco on Thursday, November 26th between 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM.
Deliver the meal(s) and spend time visiting with an older adult in their home.
Visits and deliveries should be completed between 10:30 AM – 12:30 PM.
Exact meal pick-up location will be shared in your confirmation email.

Option 2: Meal Delivery Only

Pick up meals in downtown San Francisco on Thursday, November 26th between 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM.
Deliver meals to multiple older adults who have requested delivery only (no in-home visit).
Deliveries should be completed between 10:30 AM – 12:30 PM.
Exact pick-up location will be shared in your confirmation email.

Additional Details

Family and friends are welcome to join you! At least one person in each group must have a cleared background check and volunteer orientation.

Sign up today to make Thanksgiving brighter for older adults in San Francisco!

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.title: San Francisco Critical Mass (Last Friday of the Month)
events.description:
San Francisco Critical Mass (Last Friday of the Month)
SF Critical Mass
Critical Mass is a mass bicycle ride that takes place on the last Friday of each month in San Francisco. Meet and 6pm, ride at 6:30 pm from Embarcadero Plaza (foot of Market Street) and in cities around the world. Everyone is invited. No one is in charge. Bring your bike.
Please Note: Critical Mass tends to practice extreme bike power by taking to the streets and riding in the car lanes causing endless annoyance to motorists.
In San Francisco especially, this event can get HUGE. Consider this is fair warning to stay away from driving in the downtown SF area on the last Friday of every month.

Is this comedy show really free?
Yes! Just make sure to RSVP to get on the guestlist. You must be 21+.
Tell me about the one-item minimum.
In order to hook you up with this free comedy show, there’s one-item minimum purchase per person, but it’s super affordable (and way cheaper than a traditional two-drink minimum at a bar!)
Do I need a medical marijuana card?
Nope! All you need to be is 21+ and have a valid ID.
Do I have to smoke during the show?
Nope! You can smoke, dab, eat a gummy.. whatever you want! Or you can just enjoy the show. The one-item minimum purchase still applies. So buy something and a give it to a friend! If you do decide to consume onsite, just make sure to take is slow and know your body and your limits.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

de Young Museum
Located in beautiful Golden Gate Park, the de Young Museum is a landmark art museum founded in 1895. Your visit includes a whirlwind trip around the world as the museum’s collections feature priceless treasures and works of arts from the 17th through the 20th centuries from the Americas, textile arts, and art of Africa and Oceania.
Free Admission Day: de Young
First Tuesday of the month
On the first Tuesday of every month, admission to the permanent galleries is free (special exhibition fees still apply).

Free Things to See at the de Young
Even if you don’t attend on a free day, make sure to head up to the gorgeous glass-walled Hamon Observation Tower which offers stunning 360-degree panoramic views of downtown San Francisco, Golden Gate Park, the Bay, and the Marin headlands.
Also, stroll through the whimsical Barbro Osher Sculpture Garden to see modern works and James Turrel’s site-specific sculpture Skyspace.
Access to both the Observation Tower and the Sculpture Garden are free to the public. Please note, the Tower Observation Level closes one hour before the museum closes.

events.title: $1.50 Admission Day for Ripley’s Believe It or Not!’s Final Day in SF
events.venue: Ripley’s Believe It or Not Odditorium
events.description:
Google MapsRipley’s Believe It or Not! is closing its San Francisco Odditorium at Fisherman’s Wharf on Dec. 1, 2026, ending nearly 60 years of strange sights at 175 Jefferson St. The attraction first opened on Feb. 2, 1967, and it’s sending things off with a suitably weird farewell.
On its final day, admission will cost just $1.50 for adults and 75 cents for kids, matching the original 1967 ticket prices. Want to visit before then? Ripley’s is also offering $19.67 admission on Thursdays during its final weeks.
The museum is auctioning off select exhibits and artifacts through a silent auction that stays open until closing. Among the oddities up for grabs are a Golden Gate Bridge made on the head of a pin, toothpick replicas of the bridge, Joe DiMaggio’s crutches, a chicken-wire portrait of Janis Joplin, a matchstick cable car and even a fur-covered fish. There’s also a 1989 Emmy tied to coverage of the Loma Prieta earthquake and World Series.

The building is already being marketed for lease, so the future of this longtime Wharf attraction remains up in the air.
H/t SF Chronicle

No pens, no paper.

Black Hammer Brewing Company brews and serves award-winning gluten-removed beers that are indistinguishable from conventional gluten-containing brews. We are dog friendly and offer indoor and heated outdoor seating with tons of street parking.
Get to enjoy their award-winning beers while enjoying the night with friends!

events.title: Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

This free, participatory event has been a staple at La Peña Cultural Center for 12 years due to its incredible fun, and recurs every 1st and 3rd Sunday of each month.
Come enjoy the Afro-Cuban folkloric drums, dances, and songs of rumba. Rumba is the word used for a group of related, community-oriented, music and dance styles in Cuba.
Rumba developed in rural Cuba, with strong influences from African drumming and Spanish poetry and singing.

Come play, sing, dance, or simply watch and enjoy.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
San Francisco Botanical Garden’s Free Day (2nd Tuesdays)
Saxon Holt / SF Botanical Gardens
The San Francisco Botanical Garden is one of the most diverse gardens in the world. A unique urban oasis, the garden is a living museum within Golden Gate Park, offering 55 acres of both landscaped gardens and open spaces, and showcasing over 9,000 different kinds of plants from around the world.
One of the most beautiful spots is the Japanese-design inspired “Moon Viewing Garden,” (pictured above) located in the Mild-Temperate Climate section in the Northwest portion of the gardens. [view map]
The garden is always free for San Francisco residents, but visitors can also enjoy this treasure for free on the second Tuesday of every month; plus it’s free on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day for everyone.

Early bird? Come by any day and get in for free from 7:30-9 am.

events.description:
K. ShuckSan Francisco Poet Laureate emerita Kim Shuck, poet Lauren Ito and special guests celebrate Shuck’s new collection November Dance Shirt at SFPL’s Monthly poetry reading.
Kim Shuck was San Francisco’s seventh Poet Laureate. Her poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco. Her most recent book of poetry, November Dance Shirt, was published in 2026, and her book of essays, Noodle, Rant, Tangent, was published in 2022. In her term as Poet Laureate, she hosted scores of free poetry and art workshops for all ages at neighborhood libraries and schools and worked closely with San Francisco Public Library and the San Francisco Arts Commission to launch major citywide initiatives to honor Native American Indigenous Peoples’ heritage.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Hanukkah Klezmer Party with Veretski Pass
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCookie Segelstein
Celebrate Hanukkah with a rollicking klezmer concert at the Jazzschool, presented by legendary Bay Area klezmer trio Veretski Pass. Dust off your dancing shoes and come ready to move to the driving rhythms of traditional Jewish, Ukrainian, and Polish music, as well as original compositions and spirited improvisations in the klezmer tradition. Often raucous, always danceable!
Drawing on centuries-old Eastern European traditions, Veretski Pass offers a unique and exciting combination of virtuosic musicianship and raw energy that has excited audiences internationally for more than two decades. Instrumental in co-creating the “klezmer revival,” a movement which began in the 1970s with the goal of reviving Eastern European Jewish music, the band has performed and recorded hundreds of pieces of Jewish music, drawing on a vast array of sources, including contemporary and 19th-century ethnographic collections.

Performing on original instruments in an unbound, energetic “village style,” Veretski Pass has not only preserved, but reimagined, recomposed, and rearranged Jewish music from Ukraine, Poland, Carpathian-Ruthenia, Bessarabia, and Romania, enhancing and enriching modern klezmer music.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.title: SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

The Cow Palace, 2600 Geneva Avenue, Daly City, CA

events.title: Santa Skivvies 2026: Holiday Underwear Run Through the Castro
events.description:
Roxane Chicoine, SF AIDS Foundation
Sleigh, boots! Get ready for Christmas chaos in the Castro at Santa Skivvies Run.

Santa Skivvies Run is where hundreds of scantily clad Santas take over the Castro for a one-mile holiday dash to raise funds for San Francisco AIDS Foundation. Whether this is your annual tradition or your very first time, it’s a very silly, very San Francisco way to bring in the holidays.
On event day, arrive early to check out Santa’s Village before the run kicks off. Whether you run, walk, scooter, skip or skate, you can wear your favorite festive skivvies or holiday costume. After the course, stick around for Santa’s Drag Show and awards ceremony. Organizers will provide changing booths, a gear check, glam stations and plenty of selfie opportunities. It’s all about dropping trou, raising funds and supporting community health services!

freeoaklandup
Free Oakland UP, a Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, is open Fridays through Sundays from 12–4 PM, offering free materials for art, collage, and junk journals such as ephemera, electronics parts, books, and household goods. Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.

_Free Oakland UP is open Friday to Sunday, 12-4, with new treasures and plants added weekly. Outside: everything is FREE, take as much as you want except my tables, bins and shelves. Plants and select treasures are for sale to help pay for rent and expenses. Thank you for keeping treasures out of the landfill._

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

The Downtown express route make stops at the Presidio Transit Center on the Main Post, the Letterman District, Union Street/Van Ness Avenue, Embarcadero BART, and the Transbay Terminal.

It’s free for Presidio Employees and Residents every day with an appropriate boarding pass. Connecting service to Caltrain is available.
The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.
Around the Park (Every Day – 2 Routes)

The Crissy Field Route serves the northern Presidio including the Main Post, Golden Gate Bridge, Fort Scott and Letterman District

SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerAdam ShulmanJoin pianist Adam Shulman and his trio at the Jazzschool for a cozy holiday tribute to Bay Area jazz legend Vince Guaraldi and his iconic soundtrack to Charles Schulz’s 1965 TV special, A Charlie Brown Christmas. This event features two showtimes: an earlier family concert with a shortened runtime from 5:30-7pm, and a regular concert at 8pm.
Among the most beloved holiday albums of all time, A Charlie Brown Christmas has been certified Triple Platinum, was voted into the GRAMMY Hall of Fame in 2007, and was added to the Library of Congress’ National Recording Registry’s list of “culturally, historically, or aesthetically important” American recordings.

The album features a series of Christmas standards, including the Guaraldi originals “Christmas Time Is Here” and “Skating,” classic holiday songs like “O Tannenbaum” and “What Child Is This,” and the quintessential Peanuts Christmas tune, “Linus and Lucy.”
Pianist, composer, and arranger Adam Shulman has been a staple of the San Francisco jazz scene since he moved to the city in 2002. As a music student at UC Santa Cruz, Shulman studied jazz piano with the late, beloved piano master Smith Dobson, going on to work with internationally renowned artists such as Stefon Harris, Miguel Zenón, Luciana Souza, Paula West, Larry Coryell, Bobby Hutcherson, and the Glenn Miller Orchestra.

events.title: San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
events.description:
San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

events.description:
SF’s 42nd Annual Great Dickens Christmas Fair (Nov. 21-Dec. 20)
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair via Rich Yee
The Great Dickens Christmas Fair is a one-of-a-kind trip to Victorian London, where Christmas Eve never ends. More than 140,000 square feet of the Cow Palace transforms into a maze of lamplit streets, music halls, pubs, dance floors, and shops filled with handmade gifts. Hundreds of costumed performers bring characters from Charles Dickens’ novels and Victorian life to the streets, so you might bump into Ebenezer Scrooge, watch a scene from A Christmas Carol, or find yourself swept into a spontaneous sing-along.
The Fair is a longtime Bay Area holiday tradition, with plenty to explore beyond the theatrical performances. Browse artisan shops, grab a bite or a hot drink, catch live music, learn a few Victorian dance steps, or settle into a pub for a pint. There are also family-friendly shows, activities, and a miniature live steam train in the Victoria Station lobby. Costumes are encouraged but not required, so feel free to dress the part or simply wander through 19th-century London in your regular clothes.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Located in beautiful Golden Gate Park, the de Young Museum is a landmark art museum founded in 1895. Free Admission Day: de Young
First Tuesday of the month
On the first Tuesday of every month, admission to the permanent galleries is free (special exhibition fees still apply).

Free Things to See at the de Young
Even if you don’t attend on a free day, make sure to head up to the gorgeous glass-walled Hamon Observation Tower which offers stunning 360-degree panoramic views of downtown San Francisco, Golden Gate Park, the Bay, and the Marin headlands.
Also, stroll through the whimsical Barbro Osher Sculpture Garden to see modern works and James Turrel’s site-specific sculpture Skyspace.
Access to both the Observation Tower and the Sculpture Garden are free to the public. Please note, the Tower Observation Level closes one hour before the museum closes.

The San Francisco Botanical Garden is one of the most diverse gardens in the world. A unique urban oasis, the garden is a living museum within Golden Gate Park, offering 55 acres of both landscaped gardens and open spaces, and showcasing over 9,000 different kinds of plants from around the world.
One of the most beautiful spots is the Japanese-design inspired “Moon Viewing Garden,” (pictured above) located in the Mild-Temperate Climate section in the Northwest portion of the gardens. [view map]
The garden is always free for San Francisco residents, but visitors can also enjoy this treasure for free on the second Tuesday of every month; plus it’s free on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day, and New Year’s Day for everyone.

events.title: Performing Arts Showcase
events.description:
On Friday, November 13, from 5–8 pm, Fulton Plaza will come alive beneath the dazzling SPECTRA lights for the holiday season’s Performing Arts Showcase, a celebration bringing together some of downtown’s most exciting performing arts organizations for one unforgettable evening.
Guests will be treated to a dynamic lineup of live performances of what’s on stage Fall 2026-Winter 2027. Expect short works from the San Francisco Opera, San Francisco Ballet musicians, San Francisco Conservatory of Music, the African American Shakespeare Company, RAWdance, and more. From powerful voices and sweeping orchestral music to captivating movement and theatrical performances, the showcase offers a little bit of everything — and is a memorable way to launch the holiday season.
This event is free, RSVP here. Happening rain or shine, there will be both bleacher seating and street-level/ADA accessible seating.
The event will also feature a post-show reception with an opportunity to mingle with the performing arts organizations, ticket sales, ticket raffles from the SF Symphony and Orpheum Theatre, and bites and drinks for purchase.

Thank you to event sponsors: Avenue Greenlight, Civic Center Community Benefit District, Illuminate, and the San Francisco Public Library

events.title: Moving San Francisco: SFMTA Photos 1903-Now
events.description: Moving San Francisco: Views from the SFMTA Photo Archive 1903 – Now at City Hall features, “an exhibition that celebrates the history of Muni and the evolution of our city with a collection of images from the SFMTA Photo Archive.” From the Francisco Arts Commission (SFAC), in partnership with the San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency’s (SFMTA) Photo Archive, Moving San Francisco will be on display on the Ground Floor and North Light Court at City Hall through November 25, 2026.

events.title: Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting 2026
events.description:
Join us for a festive evening at Civic Center Plaza as we illuminate the holiday season! The annual Civic Center Plaza Tree Lighting event returns December 2, 4-7pm! Add this fun, free, family-friendly event to your holiday calendar; featuring festive performances, with the night’s lineup including music, performances, and appearances from The Tap Dancing Christmas Trees, Christmas VIPs and the man-of-the-hour: Santa!
The event also features “snow” flurries, where kids (and kids at heart) can twirl and dance through the falling snow, while in the Makers Village, SF Etsy will lead holiday-themed activities and the San Francisco Public Library will host a book giveaway. Bites will be available for purchase, along with a full bar featuring seasonal favorites.
The event takes place across from an illuminated City Hall in Civic Center Plaza. Event begins promptly at 4pm, with the lighting of Civic Center’s 50-foot noble fir at 5:30pm. Happening rain or shine!
See some footage from years prior here!

events.title: Bhangra & Beats Night Market
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
San Francisco’s biggest South Asian celebration is back, and for the first time ever, it lands at Yerba Buena Gardens, one of downtown’s most iconic arts and cultural destinations.
On July 24 and November 13, Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane will transform into a vibrant, open-air celebration of music, dance, food, and culture—bringing together community, creativity, and connection in the heart of downtown.
As the only outdoor celebration of its size and scale in the Bay Area dedicated to South Asian culture, Bhangra & Beats continues to create a space that is both rooted in tradition and alive with the energy of the Bay.
At the heart of it all is the vibrant Bhangra & Beats atmosphere, a family-friendly celebration where traditional Punjabi rhythms meet Bay Area energy. Non Stop Bhangra collective will once again lead the experience with its signature mix of interactive dance lessons, beautiful performances, live dhol drumming, DJs, and an open dance floor, all flowing into a lively marketplace with food vendors, local makers, community activations, restaurant and bar specials, and family-friendly activities.
Come for the music, stay for the energy. Whether you’re dancing, eating, shopping, or just taking it all in, there’s something here for everyone.
